 THE HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE ALOK ARADHE  AND  THE HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR JUKANTI  Writ Appeal No.400 of 2024 JUDGMENT:
(Per the Hon'ble the Chief Justice Alok Aradhe) Mr. B.Shankar, learned counsel for the appellant.
Mr. G.Veeraswamy, learned Government Pleader for Social Welfare Department appears for respondents No.1 and 2.

Mr. Ramesh Chilla, learned counsel for respondents No.4 and 5.
2.
With consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is heard finally.

3. In this writ appeal, the appellant has assailed the validity of the order dated 03.05.2024, passed by a learned Single Judge by which writ petition preferred by the appellant viz., W.P.No.5520 of 2019 has been disposed of with liberty to the appellant to avail of the alternative remedy provided under ::2::
Regulation 3(a)(ii) of the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation, 1959 (hereinafter referred to as 'Regulation 1 of 1959').
4. Facts giving rise to filing of this appeal briefly stated are that appellant claims to be the owner and in possession of an extent of Ac.0.30 guntas of land in Survey No.136/1/1, situated at Mandamarri Town and Mandal, Adilabad District (hereinafter referred to as 'the schedule property').

sentences.text:
In the aforesaid writ petition, the appellant challenged the validity of the order dated 16.02.2019 passed by the Special Deputy Collector (TW), Adilabad Headquarters, Utnoor, Adilabad District (respondent No.2), whereby the Tahsilar, Mandamarri (respondent No.3), was directed to eject the appellant from the subject land and to hand over the said land to one Kota Laxmi (respondent No.4) and to report compliance.
::3::
5.

Learned Single Judge, by order dated 03.05.2024, disposed of the aforesaid writ petition with liberty to the appellant to take recourse to the alternative remedy of appeal provided under Regulation 1 of 1959.
In the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this appeal has been filed.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that under Regulation 3(1)(a) of Regulation 1 of 1959, any transfer of immovable property, situated in the agency tracts, by Scheduled Tribe, is null and void and an authority gets jurisdiction under Regulation 3(2)(a) of Regulation 1 of 1959 to pass an order of eviction only in case of a transfer, which is made in contravention of Regulation 3(1)(a)

sentences.text: In the instant case, no transfer of immovable property is involved and a complaint was made in which a grievance was made with regard to encroachment of the subject property.

::4 : :
Therefore, it is contended that the provisions of Regulation 1 of 1959 are not attracted to the facts of the case.

It is contended that in view of law laid down by the Supreme Court in Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks, Mumbai 1, the learned Single Judge ought to have dealt with the challenge made to the order passed by the authority under Regulation 1 of 1959.

sentences.text: 8. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondents No.4 and 5 fairly submitted that the writ petition is disposed of merely on the ground of availability of an alternative remedy.
9. We have considered the rival submissions made on both sides and perused the record.

10. Relevant portion of Regulation 3(1)(a) of Regulation 1 of 1959, is extracted below for the facility of reference:
(1998) 8 SCC 1 ::5::
"3. Transfer of immovable property by a member of a Scheduled Tribe:-
(1)(a) Notwithstanding anything in any enactment, rule or law in force in the Agency tracts any transfer or immovable property situated in the Agency tracts by Scheduled Tribe, shall be absolutely null and void, unless such transfer is made in favour of person, who is a member of a Scheduled Tribe or a society registered or deemed to be registered under the Andhra Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1964 (Act 7 of 1964)
which is composed solely of members of the Scheduled Tribes.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1964 (Act 7 of 1964)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
(b) Until the contrary is proved, any immovable property situated in the Agency tracts and in the possession of a person who is not a member of Scheduled Tribe,
shall be presumed to have been acquired by person or his presumed to have been acquired by person or his predecessor in possession through transfer made to him by a member of a Scheduled Tribe.

::6::
(c) Where a person intending to sell his land is not able to effect such sale, by reason of the fact that no member of a Scheduled Tribe is willing to purchase the land or is willing to purchase the land on the terms offered by such person, then such person may apply to the Agency, the Agency Divisional Officer or any other prescribed officer Kompalli Ramesh Kumar vs The State Of Telangana on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192517601/
2 of the acquisition of such land by the State Government, and the Agent.

sentences.text:
Agency Divisional Officer or the prescribed officer, as the case may be, may by order, take over such land on payment of compensation in accordance with the principles specified in Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Ceiling on Agricultural Holding Act,
1961 (Act X of 1961), and such land shall thereupon vest in the State Government free from all encumbrances and shall be disposed of in favour of members of the Scheduled Tribes or a society registered or deemed to be registered under the Andhra Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1964 (Act 7 of 1964) composed solely of members ::7::
of the Scheduled Tribes or in such other manner and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed."
11.

sentences.text: In the instant case, from a perusal of the proceeding before the Special Deputy Collector, it is evident that the grievance made in the proceeding is with regard to encroachment of the land and not with regard to sale of immovable property.
Therefore, prima facie the provisions of Regulation 1 of 1959 do not apply to the fact situation of the case.

However, since the learned Single Judge has not dealt with the challenge made to the order dated 16.02.2019, passed by the Special Deputy Collector on merits, in the clear facts of the case, we deem it appropriate to remit the matter to the learned Single Judge for adjudication afresh.

12. Therefore, order dated 03.05.2024, passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P.No.5520 of 2019,
is set aside and the learned Single Judge is requested to deal with the challenge ::8::
made to the impugned order dated order dated 16.02.2019, passed by the Special Deputy Collector, on merits.
12. Accordingly, the Writ Appeal is disposed of.
No costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, stand closed.
